Thanks everyone for joining. Notes and decisions below (copied out of the call transcript):

1) Egress zoning:
- Control plane telemetry (control plane heartbeats, model management calls, health pings) will originate from a management subnet. Redwood will accept those over a private peering interface; no public egress is required for control plane.
- Customer data (inference payloads, logs with PII) must never egress to Redwood-hosted public endpoints. Echelon will host a relay (egress translator) in their VPC that performs TLS-terminated forwarding to Redwood dedicated endpoints over an IPsec tunnel.

2) Failover behavior (routing-failover-matrix.xlsx):
- Primary path: egress translator in us-west-2 -> Redwood ingress relay in us-west-2.
- On primary relay failure: egress translator will attempt immediate TCP failover to secondary relay in us-east-1 (per routing matrix). Data will be marked in-flight and routed out-of-region; Echelon confirmed they accept cross-region egress for retries with the exception of PHI-bearing payloads (those must queue and wait for primary).
- Circuit-level heartbeat and a 10s retry window was agreed for non-PHI payloads.

3) Observability & evidence:
- Redwood will provide a daily audit bundle (TLS session metadata, message digests, timestamps) to Echelon S3 for 90-day retention as part of the onboarding.
- For SOC2 audits, Redwood will share redacted request traces and attestations on request; PII/PHI will be filtered before transfer.

4) Action items:
- Echelon to produce a short list of PHI-classified endpoints and sample payloads (Priya).
- Redwood (Aditya) to update the routing-failover-matrix with circuit heartbeat thresholds and tie into our health-checking policy.
- Kim to drop an updated diagram showing IPSec tunnel endpoints and NAT behavior.

Next steps: we'll circulate the updated diagram and the revised failover matrix by EOD tomorrow. If anything below disagrees with your notes, please flag.

--
Michael Grant
